simple.meaning: קוֹף (qôwph) is a Hebrew word meaning “a monkey.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: קוֹף (H6971) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 10:22, with occurrences in 1 Kings, 2 Chronicles.

simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in קוֹף (H6971) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: קוֹף (qôwph) / H6971 is traced through 1 Kings 10:22, 2 Chronicles 9:21 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6971. qoph [ קוֺף ] noun [masculine] ape , so Vrss, ᵐ5 πίθηκοι (omitted by ᵐ5 B in Kings) (foreign word; probably = Sanskrit kapi , id. ; Egyptian as loan-word gôfë WMM As.u.Eur.95 , gi'f Erman ZMG xlvi (1892), 121 ; Greek κῆβος, κῆπος is of Egyptian origin according to Lewy Fremdw. 6 ); — plural קֹפִים 1Kin 10:22 = קוֺפִים 2Chr 9:21 , brought to Solomon [from southeast] by Phoenician fleet; compare Arabic proverb 'donum regionis Jemen simiae sunt,' Frey Provv.iii.3160 .

occurrences.englishText: For the king had a fleet of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet. Once every three years the fleet of Tarshish came, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
For the king had ships that went to Tarshish with Huram’s servants. Once every three years, the ships of Tarshish came bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
